data.gender_notes: Kesar is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word 'Kesara', meaning 'gold' or 'amber'. Kesar is a name of reverence and royalty. In Hindu mythology, Kesara is also the name of a sacred tree known for its healing properties. The name is associated with courage, strength, and wisdom. The name Kesar carries the meaning “Gold, Amber, King” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Kesar usually hope their child will grow to embody gold, amber, king and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name 'Kesar' holds a special place in Hindu culture due to its association with the precious metal, gold. Gold symbolizes wealth, power, and status in Indian society. Furthermore, it is believed that Goddess Lakshmi, the goddess of wealth, resides in gold. Hence, the name 'Kesar' reflects prosperity, success, and fortunate beginnings.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name 'Kesar' signifies the purity and radiance of the soul. Hindu mythology describes the divine nectar, Amrit, as being golden in color. By carrying the name 'Kesar', an individual can be reminded of their inner golden Divine essence. Additionally, the spiritual power of the name is amplified when used in mantra and meditation practices, as 'Om Kesaro Namah'. It serves as a reminder of the Supreme Consciousness that resides within each soul, illuminating the darkness and guiding the way towards self-realization.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Kesar: The name Kesar is derived from the Sanskrit word 'kesara', meaning 'saffron' in color. Symbolically, it represents purity, enlightenment, and spiritual growth, as saffron is the color of the robe worn by ascetics and gods in Hinduism.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Kesar was a famous king in the Gupta Empire. The name Kesar carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
